top_story: Trump’s 22 September UN threat to “annihilate” Iran sharply raised regional escalation risk just as Yemen’s war was widening along the Red Sea coast, where Houthi gains have killed hundreds and displaced more than 100,000 people. The timing matters because maximalist U.S. rhetoric strengthens the confrontation frame in which Iran-aligned actors operate, increasing the chance that local battlefields absorb broader strategic pressure. In Gaza, students returning on 23 September to tent schools after three years of devastation underscores that even where front lines stabilize, civilian life remains defined by ruin, crowding, and institutional collapse. The regional picture is one of conflicts feeding each other politically while ordinary people bear the lasting costs through displacement, shattered services, and narrowing prospects for recovery.
